newsitem.title: UK: Copper bursts higher on LME, heads toward $1,970.
newsitem.headline: Copper bursts higher on LME, heads toward $1,970.

text.p: Copper sliced through an interim layer of resistance on Thursday afternoon, setting the scene for a challenge of the top end of its month-old range, traders said.
Firmer spreads, the upcoming options expiry next week and short-covering ahead of the U.S. holiday on Monday contributed to the buoyancy.
"Tomorrow will be key with stocks...If copper comes in lower than than the expected rise of 10,000 tonnes we could see a test of $1,970," said Robin Bahr, analyst at broker Billiton.
Copper's strength injected some life in the other metals, which all moved higher in sympathy.
Three months copper hopped above the $1,950 interim resistance level as spreads firmed, ending the kerb $16 stronger at $1,959 per tonne after hitting a two-week high of $1,964.
Spreads widened, with cash/threes last trading at a $44 backwardation compared to $37 on Wednesday.
Tightness had been expected since players who had gone short in early June in the wake of the Sumitomo scandal will need to cover or roll over their three-month positions.
But progress on the upside may be difficult as selling is expected from banks who are said to have taken over Sumitomo's long position, Bahr added.
Copper last touched $1,970 on August 1 and has since been trapped in a range with $1,900 as a floor.
Traders were also watching for strike action pegged for Saturday at Chile's Salvador mine and an output stoppage at Gold Fields's copper smelter in Namibia.

Aluminium followed copper higher, cruising past $1,490 resistance on its way to confronting the $1,500 level, the day's high. Three month prices finished the afternoon kerb at $1,497, a gain of $10.50.
Nearby physical demand is said to be low but recent price dips have spurred customers to book forward metal, traders said.
Nickel climbed with the others, but peaked at $7,430, about $20 shy of a key resistance level. This represented the third failure in four days to surmount the $7,450 level.
Three months metal finished the day at $7,425, a gain of $75.
Lead hardly moved, trapped within a $2 range, ending the day at $804.50, a loss of 50 cents.
"The $806 level is important resistance and a close above signals a rally towards $822," said Harry Creates, chartist for broker AMT, in a commentary.
Tin shot higher, surmounting resistance at $6,200 and breaking out of its month-old range.
It finished the kerb at $6,215, up $40, with next resistance pegged at $6,250, according to Creates.
Zinc ended the day slightly higher, closing at $1,029.50, up $5.50.
Noranda Inc said it would lose 40,000 tonnes of contained zinc metal in concentrates due to the reduction in output at its Brunswick mine in Canada.
Alloy finished at $1,296/97 versus $1,285/90.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8065
